title: A damaged boat was the one the king did not take.
subtitle: The first hidden reason
then: Allah showed Al-Khidr the hidden reasons. A king who was {trap}one of the oppressors{/trap} seized every good boat by force. Making it look faulty meant {reward}its poor owners who had nothing else could benefit from it{/reward}. It was also said they were orphans.
now: You did not get the bigger flat, the flashier job, the car you wanted. Years later you see what that bigger thing would have cost you. {idea}A small dent can keep the whole boat safe.{/idea}
old: Every setback is just a loss.
new: Some damage is protection I cannot see yet.
try: Recall one past disappointment that later turned out to protect you, and thank Allah for it.

title: His believing parents were spared what was coming.
subtitle: The second hidden reason
then: Their love for him {trap}might make them follow him in disbelief{/trap}. Qatadah said his parents rejoiced at his birth and grieved at his death, and had he lived he would have caused their ruin. He said: {reward}let a man be content with the decree of Allah{/reward}. The hadith says Allah decrees nothing for the believer except it is good for him.
now: You lost something you loved and begged Allah to keep. You still miss it. {idea}You may never see the reason in this life.{/idea} But the believer's loss is never wasted with Allah.
old: If Allah took it, He must not care about me.
new: Allah's decree for a believer is good, even when it breaks my heart.
try: Say Alhamdulillah ala kulli hal, praise to Allah in every state, once today about something painful.

title: A better child, nearer to mercy, in his place.
subtitle: Loss followed by replacement
then: Ibn Jurayj explained the replacement: {reward}a child who was better than this one, a child for whom they would feel more compassion{/reward}. The grief was real. So was {idea}what their Lord intended for them next{/idea}.
now: After a miscarriage, a lost job, a friendship that ended, the space feels empty for a long time. {idea}Allah does not take from a believer without intending something good to follow.{/idea}
old: What I lost can never be replaced.
new: Allah can give me something better after loss, in His timing.
try: Make dua today: O Allah, reward me in my loss and give me better after it.

title: Their father was righteous, so Allah guarded their treasure.
subtitle: The third hidden reason

row.title: mercy from your Lord
sub: I did it not of myself

then: Ibn Kathir says this shows {reward}a righteous person's offspring will be taken care of{/reward}, and the blessing of his worship extends to them. Ibn Abbas noted it is not said the boys themselves were righteous. Al-Khidr ended: all three were {idea}mercy from your Lord, and I did them not of my own accord{/idea}.
now: You pray at night when the house is asleep, give quietly, keep your word at work. You worry what will become of your kids. {idea}Your goodness today may be the wall that guards them long after you.{/idea}
old: My children's future depends only on what I leave them in money.
new: My righteousness can protect my children in ways I will never see.
try: Do one good deed today with the intention that Allah protects your family through it.

title: They asked about Dhul-Qarnayn. Here is his story.
subtitle: The third question answered
then: The disbelievers of Makkah had asked the People of the Book for questions to test the Prophet ﷺ. One was {idea}a man who traveled extensively throughout the earth{/idea}. The answer came as revelation: {reward}say, I will recite to you something of his story{/reward}.
now: You search for answers about life in ten browser tabs and three podcasts. {idea}The Quran says: I will recite to you.{/idea} Some answers are given, not found.
old: I have to find every answer myself.
new: Allah has already recited some answers. I can start there.
try: Before searching online about a big question today, read what the Quran says on it first.

title: Allah gave him power and the means to everything.
subtitle: Strength handed to a king
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah gave him {reward}great power{/reward}, armies and equipment, with dominion over east and west. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the means of everything meant {idea}knowledge{/idea}. Notice the verbs: {idea}We established, We gave{/idea}.
now: You got the promotion, the team, the budget. You have more say over people than ever before. {idea}It was handed to you, and it will be asked about.{/idea}
old: My position is mine because I earned it.
new: Any power I hold was given to me by Allah, as a trust.
try: Use whatever authority you have today, at home or work, to make one person's day easier.

title: He used the means. He followed a way.
subtitle: Gifts are meant to be used
then: Only three words: so he followed a way. Ibn Abbas said {idea}he followed different routes to achieve what he wanted{/idea}. Qatadah said he followed {idea}the routes and landmarks of the earth{/idea}. He was given the means, and he used them.
now: You have a skill you have not touched in years. A language, an instrument, a talent for teaching. {idea}A gift left unused is still a gift, but it does no good sitting on the shelf.{/idea}
new: A gift from Allah is meant to be used on a path.
try: Spend twenty minutes today using one skill you have been neglecting.

title: At the far west, he was given a choice about a people.
subtitle: Power tested by choice

row.title: the far west
sub: sun seems to set in the sea

then: He reached the furthest point west and {idea}saw the sun as if it were setting in the ocean{/idea}, as anyone on a coast sees. Ibn Kathir calls tales of him reaching where the sun sets in the sky {trap}not true at all{/trap}. There Allah gave him power over a people, and a choice, and {reward}his justice and faith became apparent{/reward}.
now: You are the older sibling, the manager, the parent. Someone under you messes up and you can go hard or go gentle. {idea}What you do when you could do anything shows who you are.{/idea}
old: Having power means I can do what I want.
new: Power is a test of whether I choose justice and goodness.
try: Next time you have the upper hand with someone today, choose the kinder fair option.

title: The one who does wrong answers here and to his Lord.
subtitle: Justice that remembers the Hereafter

row.title: Allah
sub: he will be returned to Him

then: His answer showed {reward}his justice and faith{/reward}. He would act against the one who {trap}persists in his disbelief and wrongdoing{/trap}, then that person would be returned to his Lord. Ibn Kathir notes this {idea}implies a confirmation of the Hereafter{/idea}, even in a king's words.
now: You get away with a shortcut at work and the boss never finds out. {idea}Earthly accounts are not the final ones.{/idea} The verse is a mirror: every one of us will be returned to our Lord.
old: If no one catches me, there is no consequence.
new: Even if I escape here, I am returned to my Lord.
try: Correct one small wrong of yours today that no one else knows about.

title: For the one who believes and does good: ease and kind words.
subtitle: How a just leader treats the good
then: For the one who believes, the reward is {reward}the best reward in the Hereafter, with Allah{/reward}. And from the king himself: {idea}we shall speak to him mild words{/idea}. Mujahid said: words of kindness.
now: The reliable colleague, the child who does what you ask, the spouse who never complains. {idea}They are the easiest to forget to thank.{/idea} Ease and gentle words are their due.
old: The good ones do not need my attention.
new: The ones doing good deserve my gentleness and ease most of all.
try: Thank the most reliable person in your life today in specific, gentle words.

title: Then he followed another way.
subtitle: After one task, the next
then: Ibn Kathir says he then {idea}traveled from the west of the earth towards the east{/idea}. Each time he passed a nation, {reward}he called them to Allah{/reward}. One mission completed simply led into the next.
now: You finished Ramadan strong, then the next month you stopped. You memorized one surah, then shelved the rest. {idea}The verse just says: then he followed another way.{/idea}
old: I have done my good deed. I can rest now.
new: Each good done opens the next road. I keep following it.
try: Pick the next small step after something good you recently finished, and start it today.

title: A people with nothing to shade them from the sun.
subtitle: In the far east
then: He reached the place where the sun rises and found a people with {trap}no buildings or trees to cover them and shade them from the heat{/trap}. Qatadah said it was mentioned they lived in a land where {trap}nothing grew{/trap}, sheltering until the sun passed its peak.
now: You complain the air conditioning is weak, that the flat is small. {idea}A roof and shade are blessings most people in history did not have.{/idea}
old: Shelter and comfort are just normal.
new: A roof over my head is a gift I easily forget.
try: Thank Allah today for your roof, then give something toward someone's shelter.

title: So it was. And We knew all that he had.
subtitle: Nothing about him was hidden
then: Mujahid and As-Suddi said this means {idea}Allah knew everything about him and his army, and nothing was hidden from Him{/idea}, even though they came from many nations and lands. As the verse says: {idea}nothing is hidden from Allah, in the earth or in the heaven{/idea}.
now: You are one face in a city of millions, one of a thousand employees. You feel lost in the crowd. {idea}Allah knows all that you have, all you do, all you carry.{/idea}
old: I am too small to be noticed in all of this.
new: Allah encompasses all of it, and me in it.
try: Tonight, tell Allah about one thing you did today that no one noticed.
